subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw standardize per-skill user preferences as a markdown sidecar, a structured config surface, or keep the current `SKILL.md`-only contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the right behavior changes skill loading precedence, prompt contents, watcher invalidation, and possibly config surface area, so automation should not pick the product contract alone.

options.title: Standardize a markdown sidecar
options.body: Adopt one documented markdown file such as `preferences.md`, load it with the selected skill, and update prompt-version/watch/test behavior around that contract.

options.title: Use structured skill config
options.body: Keep prompt guidance in `SKILL.md` and express user preferences through `skills.entries.*.config`, accepting the extra config-schema and docs burden.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Leave user conventions as manual skill-authored behavior until a stronger product need or a broader skill personalization design is approved.

recommendation.title: Standardize a markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Adopt one documented markdown file such as `preferences.md`, load it with the selected skill, and update prompt-version/watch/test behavior around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The current skill loader, prompt formatter, and docs history most strongly route this product/API choice through steipete's recent area work.
